candidate.claim: cachedIndentRegex creates the regex from cacheIndex instead of indent, so indent 1 gets {0,0}, indent 2 gets {0,1}, indent 3 gets {0,2} and any larger indent gets {0,3} instead of {0,indent}.
candidate.title: Cached indent regex uses cache index as indent

verifier.reason: The excerpt at rules.ts:9 shows createRegex(cacheIndex) with cacheIndex derived at rules.ts:6, but no provided excerpt shows any call site of cachedIndentRegex or how its callback converts the argument into a {0,N} quantifier, so the claimed {0,0}/{0,1}/{0,2}/{0,3} mapping cannot be settled without seeing the callback definitions in rules.ts beyond line 74.

candidate.claim: Lexer.lex reuses this.tokens without clearing it, so a second lex() call on the same Lexer instance appends to the first call's tokens and links instead of returning only the new result.
candidate.title: Lexer tokens accumulator never reset on reuse

verifier.reason: The constructor initializes this.tokens and its links once at Lexer.ts:32, and lex() at Lexer.ts:99 passes that same this.tokens to blockTokens without any intervening reset, so reuse appends to the prior array.

candidate.claim: Parser extension fallback uses `ret !== false || !knownList.includes(type)`, so when an extension renderer exists for an unknown token type and returns false the parser outputs empty string and continues instead of falling through to the unknown-token error.
candidate.title: Extension returning false for unknown token is swallowed

verifier.reason: Confirmed: at Parser.ts:54 the condition is true when ret===false and the type is not in the built-in list, so Parser.ts:55-56 appends '' and continues, bypassing the unknown-token error at Parser.ts:112-119; the same pattern at Parser.ts:140-142 bypasses Parser.ts:193-200.
